Excludes third-party transactions outside collaboration partners.

Restructuring and cost-reduction (Note 3.A: Transforming to a More Focused Company Program):
- Context: Post-2019 Consumer Healthcare JV and 2020 Upjohn spin-off, Pfizer is aligning its cost base/support model; certain indirect costs remained.
- Three initiatives (expected primarily 2020–2022; costs approximate):

  2) Transform commercial go-to-market: ~$1.1B (mostly cash) for centralization, digital engagement; severance/implementation costs.
  3) Optimize manufacturing network/cost reduction: ~$800M (~25% non-cash) for severance, implementation, product transfers, site exits, accelerated depreciation.

nodes.title: Taxes on Income from Continuing Operations

nodes.start_phrase:
Components of 
Income from continuing operations before provision/(benefit) for taxes on income include:
nodes.summary:
- Document section: Pfizer Inc. 2021 Form 10-K, Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements—focus on Note 4 (Other income/deductions—net) and Note 5 (Tax Matters).
- Note 4 summary:
  - Presents components of Other (income)/deductions—net for 2021, 2020, 2019. Totals: $(4,878) million (income) in 2021, $1,219 million (expense) in 2020, and $3,497 million (expense) in 2019.
  - Key drivers in 2021:
    - Large unrealized gains on equity securities (notably ~$1.6 billion from BioNTech and Cerevel).
    - Collaboration and out-licensing income, including $188 million net collaboration income from BioNTech for the COVID-19 vaccine and $97 million in milestones from multiple licensees.
    - Net periodic benefit credits (versus costs in 2020).
    - “Other, net” includes $288 million net TSA income, $166 million ViiV dividends, and a $142 million charge for contingent consideration remeasurement.
  - 2020 highlights:
    - Unrealized gains (~$405 million) from BioNTech and SpringWorks.
    - Upfront/milestone income (Biogen CK1 sale $75m; Puma Neratinib EU $40m; Lilly LOXO-292 $30m; other milestones $108m).
    - Significant intangible asset impairments: $900m IPR&D (Array), $528m Eucrisa (Anacor), $263m Hospira sterile injectables.
    - “Other, net” includes $278m ViiV dividends, $114m TSA net income, and $105m contingent consideration charges.
  - 2019 highlights:
    - Unrealized gains (~$295m) from Cortexyme and SpringWorks.
    - Milestones ($78m from Mylan for Wixela Inhub; $52m others).
    - Major impairments (~$2.8b, largely $2.6b Eucrisa).
    - Consumer Healthcare JV-related costs and $138m net losses on early debt retirement within “Other, net.”
  - Includes legal reserves for certain matters; business/legal entity alignment costs (2019) for restructuring setup; capitalized interest: $108m (2021), $96m (2020), $88m (2019).
  - Impairment charges are based on fair value estimates; certain amounts reflect a change in accounting principle.
- Note 5—Tax Matters:
  - Pre-tax income by geography:
    - 2021: U.S. $6.1b; International $18.2b (driven by Comirnaty, lower impairments, and net periodic benefit credits).
    - 2020: U.S. $(2.9)b loss; International $9.9b.
    - 2019: U.S. $7.3b; International $4.0b.
    - Year-over-year explanations:
      - 2021 vs. 2020: Shift to U.S. income and higher international income mainly from Comirnaty, lower impairments, benefit credits, and higher equity gains, partly offset by higher R&D.
      - 2020 vs. 2019: U.S. loss due to no repeat of Consumer Healthcare JV gain, higher impairments and R&D; international up due to no repeat of JV asset write-offs, lower impairments, and lower intangible amortization.
  - Provision/(benefit) for taxes on income:
    - 2021 total tax provision $1.85b; 2020 $0.37b; 2019 $0.58b, with details of U.S. and international current and deferred components and TCJA items in 2019.
    - Pfizer elected to pay the ~$15b U.S. repatriation tax (post-1986 foreign earnings) over eight years; third installment paid in 2021; fourth due April 18, 2022; remainder classified in noncurrent other taxes payable.
  - Effective tax rate (ETR) reconciliation:
    - ETRs: 7.6% (2021), 5.3% (2020), 5.2% (2019).
    - 2021 higher ETR mainly from jurisdictional mix tied to Comirnaty and lower impairment-related tax benefits, partly offset by Consumer Healthcare JV–related initiatives.

  - Detailed components of deferred tax assets/liabilities for 2021 and 2020 presented (prepaid/deferred items, inventories, intangibles, PP&E, employee benefits, NOL/credit carryforwards, investments, etc.), including GILTI-related items.
  - Net deferred tax position shifted to a $1.27b asset in 2021 from a $(3.12)b liability in 2020.
  - 2021 changes driven by Comirnaty royalty accrual timing differences, recognition of operating lease ROU liabilities, acquisition-related intangibles (Trillium), and lower deferred tax liabilities from intangible amortization.

nodes.title: Tax Rate Reconciliation
nodes.heading: B. Tax Rate Reconciliation
nodes.start_phrase:
The reconciliation of the U.S. statutory income tax rate to our ef
fective tax rate for Income from continuing operations follows:
nodes.summary:
- Covers Pfizer’s tax rate reconciliation and deferred taxes within the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.
- Tax rate reconciliation (Years ended 2019–2021): U.S. statutory tax rate of 21% reconciled to effective tax rates of 7.6% (2021), 5.3% (2020), and 5.2% (2019).
- Key drivers of the effective tax rate vs. statutory:
  - Taxation of non-U.S. operations reduces the rate (2021: -4.3 pts; 2020: -9.9 pts; 2019: -4.7 pts).
  - Tax settlements/resolution of certain positions reduce the rate (2021: -0.4; 2020: -2.7; 2019: -14.0).
  - Consumer Healthcare JV: completion increased the 2019 rate (+8.3), while 2021 initiatives decreased it (-6.0).
  - U.S. R&D credit reduces the rate (2021: -0.5; 2020: -1.4; 2019: -0.8).
  - Interest increases the rate (2021: +0.4; 2020: +1.1; 2019: +0.6).
  - TCJA impact affected 2019 only (-2.9). “All other, net” modest reductions each year.
- Explanation of non-U.S. tax effects: driven by jurisdictional mix of earnings, U.S. tax on foreign operations, tax initiatives, and changes in uncertain tax positions (excluding those in the “settlements” line). Mix can vary with operating fluctuations and strategic items (restructuring, impairments, gains/losses).
- Incentive regimes lowering the effective tax rate: Singapore (incentive rates through 2047) and Puerto Rico (tax grant expiring 2029) providing partial exemptions.
- Interest line includes changes in interest on uncertain tax positions; “All other, net” primarily routine operations.
- Deferred taxes (before jurisdictional netting):
  - 2021 totals: assets $10,446m; liabilities $(7,714)m; valuation allowance $(1,462)m; net deferred tax asset $1,269m.
  - 2020 totals: assets $9,190m; liabilities $(10,726)m; valuation allowance $(1,586)m; net deferred tax liability $(3,123)m.
  - Major components include prepaid/deferred items, inventories, intangible assets (significant liability), PP&E (liability), employee benefits, reserves, NOL/tax credits, unremitted earnings, state/local adjustments, investments, and other.
- 2021 movements: net deferred tax position improved primarily due to temporary differences from Comirnaty royalty accruals and operating lease ROU liabilities; increased deferred tax assets from Trillium intangible acquisitions; reduced deferred tax liabilities from intangible amortization.
- Deferred taxes related to GILTI are included in relevant categories.

nodes.title: Deferred Taxes
nodes.heading: C. Deferred Taxes
nodes.start_phrase: Components of our deferred tax assets and liabilities, shown before jurisdictional netting, follow:
nodes.summary:
- Reconciliation of Pfizer’s U.S. statutory tax rate (21%) to its effective tax rate for 2019–2021, showing effective rates of 7.6% (2021), 5.3% (2020), and 5.2% (2019). Key drivers include taxation of non-U.S. operations, tax settlements/resolutions, impacts from the Consumer Healthcare joint venture (completion and initiatives), U.S. R&D credits, interest, TCJA effects (2019), and other routine items.
- Detailed explanation of how the jurisdictional mix of earnings, U.S. tax on foreign operations, uncertain tax positions, valuation allowances, and operating fluctuations affect the effective tax rate, with emphasis on benefits from tax incentives in Singapore (through 2047) and Puerto Rico (grant expiring 2029).
- Breakdown of deferred tax assets and liabilities for 2021 and 2020 by category (e.g., prepaid/deferred items, inventories, intangibles, PPE, employee benefits, NOLs/credits, investments), including valuation allowances and the net position shift to a net deferred tax asset in 2021. Noted drivers include Comirnaty royalty accruals, operating lease ROU assets/liabilities, Trillium intangible acquisition, amortization of intangibles, Consumer Healthcare JV initiatives, and pension asset performance. GILTI-related deferred taxes are included in relevant categories.
- Classification of noncurrent deferred tax assets and liabilities, availability and expirations (indefinite to 2041) of carryforwards, IRC Section 382 limitations, and disclosure that $55.0 billion of foreign earnings are indefinitely reinvested (no U.S. tax provision recorded; hypothetical liability not practicable to estimate).
- Tax contingencies and uncertain tax positions: balances of net unrecognized tax benefits ($4.5B in 2021; $4.3B in 2020), related assets recorded, and note that recognition would mostly affect the effective tax rate. Reconciliation of gross unrecognized tax benefits for 2019–2021, reflecting changes from current/prior-period positions, settlements, FX, acquisitions/divestitures (including Upjohn separation), and other items.
- Interest on unrecognized tax benefits recorded primarily in the tax provision, with net increases in 2021 ($108M) and 2020 ($89M), and a net decrease in 2019 ($564M) due to an IRS settlement; disclosure of gross accrued interest balances and related cash payments.
- Cross-references to other notes for additional details (e.g., Note 5A, 1Q, 11A, 15).

nodes.title: Tax Contingencies
nodes.heading: D. Tax Contingencies
nodes.start_phrase:
For a description of our accounting policies associated with accounting for income tax contingencies, see 
Note 1Q.
nodes.summary:
- Focus area: Income tax-related notes in Pfizer’s consolidated financial statements, covering deferred taxes, carryforwards, unremitted earnings, tax contingencies, and uncertain tax positions.

- Deferred taxes:
  - 2021 increase in net deferred tax liabilities driven primarily by operating lease ROU assets (see Note 15).
  - 2021 decrease in net deferred tax assets due to favorable pension plan asset performance (see Note 11A).
  - 2021 decrease in net deferred tax liabilities also tied to initiatives related to the Consumer Healthcare JV executed in Q3 2021.
  - Balances: 2021 noncurrent deferred tax assets and other noncurrent tax assets $1.6 billion; noncurrent deferred tax liabilities $0.3 billion. 2020 comparable amounts: $0.9 billion assets; $4.1 billion liabilities.
  - Net deferred tax amounts in 2021 and 2020 reduced by $3.0 billion of unrecognized tax benefits where loss/credit carryforwards are available to offset disallowances.

- Tax attributes and carryforwards:
  - Carryforwards include net operating and capital losses, general business credits, foreign tax credits, and charitable contributions.
  - Expiration: some indefinite; others expire 2022–2041.
  - Certain U.S. NOLs and credits subject to IRC Section 382 limitations.

- Unremitted earnings:
  - No U.S. tax provision on $55.0 billion of unremitted earnings of international subsidiaries as of December 31, 2021, as these are intended to be indefinitely reinvested.
  - Not practicable to estimate a hypothetical deferred tax liability; amounts subject to change based on operations, statutory statements, tax return finalization, and audits; analysis updated regularly.

- Tax contingencies and uncertain tax positions (see Note 1Q for policies):
  - Net unrecognized tax benefits (excluding interest): $4.5 billion at December 31, 2021; $4.3 billion at December 31, 2020.
  - Tax assets for uncertain tax positions represent potential relief from double taxation via competent authority processes; recoverability depends on payments and treaty-based recoveries.
  - Assets associated with uncertain tax positions: $1.5 billion at 12/31/21 (included in noncurrent deferred tax assets and other noncurrent tax assets $1.4 billion and other taxes payable $105 million); $1.3 billion at 12/31/20 (in noncurrent deferred tax assets and other noncurrent tax assets $1.1 billion, noncurrent deferred tax liabilities $122 million, and other taxes payable $46 million).
  - Substantially all unrecognized tax benefits, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate.

- Reconciliation of gross unrecognized tax benefits (2019–2021):
  - Ending balances: $6,068 million (2021); $5,595 million (2020); $5,381 million (2019).
  - Changes reflect positions taken in current and prior periods, settlements with U.S. and foreign authorities, impacts of divestitures (notably Upjohn in 2020), foreign exchange, cash payments/reductions of tax attributes, and statute lapses.
  - Classification details:
    - 2021: Income taxes payable $19 million; Other current assets $42 million; Noncurrent deferred tax assets and other noncurrent tax assets $3.0 billion; Noncurrent deferred tax liabilities $5 million; Other taxes payable $3.0 billion.
    - 2020: Income taxes payable $34 million; Noncurrent deferred tax assets and other noncurrent tax assets $18 million; Noncurrent deferred tax liabilities $3.0 billion; Other taxes payable $2.5 billion.

- Interest on unrecognized tax benefits:
  - Recorded in the tax provision.
  - Net interest changes: +$108 million (2021); +$89 million (2020); −$564 million (2019, primarily from an IRS settlement).
  - Gross accrued interest totaled $601 million at December 31, 2021 (decrease of $1 million from cash payments).

nodes.title: Uncertain Tax Positions
nodes.heading: Uncertain Tax Positions
nodes.start_phrase:
As tax law is complex and often subject to varied interpretations, it is uncertain whether some of our tax
 positions will be sustained upon audit.
nodes.summary:
- Deferred taxes: 2021 net deferred tax liabilities rose mainly due to recognition of operating lease right-of-use assets; net deferred tax assets declined due to favorable pension asset performance. A separate initiative tied to the Consumer Healthcare JV reduced net deferred tax liabilities in 2021. Noncurrent deferred tax assets were $1.6 billion and liabilities $0.3 billion in 2021 (vs. $0.9 billion assets and $4.1 billion liabilities in 2020). The company has loss and credit carryforwards (some subject to IRC Section 382) with indefinite lives or expirations through 2041.
- Unremitted foreign earnings: $55.0 billion of international subsidiary earnings are intended to be indefinitely reinvested; no U.S. tax provision recorded and a hypothetical deferred tax liability is not practicable to estimate.
- Uncertain tax positions: Net unrecognized tax benefits (excluding interest) were $4.5 billion in 2021 ($4.3 billion in 2020). Assets associated with uncertain tax positions totaled $1.5 billion in 2021, largely in noncurrent deferred tax assets; most unrecognized tax benefits, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate. A rollforward shows 2021 ending gross unrecognized tax benefits of $6.1 billion, reflecting current/prior-period position changes, settlements, FX, and other items.
- Interest and penalties: Net interest on unrecognized tax benefits increased $108 million in 2021 ($89 million in 2020); accrued interest totaled $601 million at year-end 2021 ($493 million in 2020). Penalties are not significant.
- Audit status and outlook: The IRS issued RARs for 2011–2015 (under appeal); 2016–2018 are under audit; 2019–2021 are open. Major audits are also open in Canada, Europe, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. It is reasonably possible gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease by up to $75 million within 12 months due to settlements or statute expirations, though timing and outcomes are uncertain.
- Taxes in other comprehensive income: The tax provision/(benefit) on OCI was $71 million in 2021, $(227) million in 2020, and $178 million in 2019, with components from foreign currency translation, derivative instruments, available-for-sale securities, and benefit plans. Taxes are not provided on translation adjustments for indefinitely held foreign investments.
- Accumulated other comprehensive loss (AOCL): Net AOCL was $(5.9) billion at December 31, 2021, comprised of foreign currency translation $(6.2) billion, derivatives $0.1 billion, available-for-sale securities $(0.2) billion, and benefit plans $0.4 billion. Changes reflect annual OCI activity, the Upjohn distribution, hedging impacts, and an accounting principle change.

Uses derivatives and foreign currency debt to mitigate remeasurement and translation impacts. Hedges a portion of forecasted intercompany inventory sales up to two years and may hedge net investments in foreign subsidiaries under certain conditions.
- Hedge accounting policies:
  - Fair value hedges: Gains/losses on FX or interest rate contracts and the hedged items’ offset recorded in earnings.
  - Cash flow hedges: Gains/losses recorded in OCI and reclassified to earnings when the hedged transactions affect earnings; certain excluded components amortized to earnings.
  - Net investment hedges: FX gains/losses on qualifying instruments recorded in OCI (foreign currency translation adjustments) and reclassified to earnings upon sale or substantial liquidation of the net investment.
  - Non-designated FX contracts: Gains/losses recognized immediately in earnings to offset related balance sheet exposures.
- Interest rate risk: Manages exposure via interest rate swaps to hedge fixed-rate fair value risk or convert variable-rate exposures to fixed, primarily on U.S. dollar fixed-rate debt; fair value hedge accounting applied with changes recognized in earnings alongside hedged item offsets.

- Debt retirements: Pfizer repurchased multiple outstanding notes in 2019–2020 (including $1.15B 1.95% notes due 2021, $342M 5.80% notes due 2023, $1.065B due 2047, and €1.1B 5.75% euro debt due 2021), recording net losses in Other (income)/deductions—net; 2019 actions included termination of related cross-currency swaps.
- Derivative and hedging program overview: Manages foreign exchange and interest rate risks using derivatives and foreign currency debt to mitigate remeasurement and translation impacts.
- Foreign exchange risk management: Primary currencies include euro, U.K. pound, Japanese yen, and Canadian dollar; hedges a portion of forecasted intercompany inventory sales in EUR, JPY, CAD, CNY, GBP, and AUD for up to two years; may hedge net investments in foreign subsidiaries.
- Interest rate risk management: Uses interest rate swaps to hedge fixed-rate exposures or convert variable to fixed; activity primarily hedges U.S. dollar fixed‑rate debt.
- Hedge accounting policies:
  - Fair value hedges: Gains/losses recognized in earnings with offsetting impact from hedged items.
  - Cash flow hedges: Gains/losses recorded in OCI and reclassified to earnings when the hedged transactions affect earnings; certain excluded amounts amortized into earnings.
  - Net investment hedges: FX gains/losses recorded in OCI (foreign currency translation) and reclassified upon sale/substantial liquidation; includes use of foreign currency borrowings.
  - Non-designated FX contracts: Gains/losses recognized immediately in earnings to offset underlying exposures.
- Quantitative disclosures (as of Dec 31, 2021 and 2020): Fair values and notional amounts reported for FX and interest rate derivatives, both designated and non-designated; notional FX contracts hedging intercompany inventory sales were ~$4.8B (2021) and ~$5.0B (2020).
- Results of hedging activities (2021 vs. 2020): Tables summarize gains/losses recognized in Other (income)/deductions—net, OCI, and amounts reclassified to earnings (including Cost of sales); expectation to reclassify a pre‑tax gain of ~$362M from OCI to income within 12 months; maximum hedge horizon ~21 years (foreign currency debt).
- Net investment hedges via borrowings: Foreign currency short‑term borrowings (~$1.1B carrying value at 12/31/21) and long‑term debt ($844M at 12/31/21 vs. $2.1B at 12/31/20) used as hedges.
- Fair value hedge basis adjustments: Cumulative adjustments to long‑term debt disclosed for active and discontinued hedge relationships, with carrying amounts and cumulative adjustments presented for 2021 and 2020.
- Credit risk: Ongoing monitoring of customer, financial institution, and investment portfolio credit risk; generally no collateral required from customers; references to additional receivables information.

nodes.summary:
- Scope: Pfizer Inc.’s 2021 Form 10-K, Note 10A (Identifiable Intangible Assets), summarizing composition, balances, changes, and accounting treatment of intangible assets as of December 31, 2021 and 2020.

- Balances and composition:
  - Finite-lived intangible assets (developed technology rights, brands, licensing agreements/other) and indefinite-lived assets (brands, IPR&D, licensing agreements/other) are presented with gross carrying amounts, accumulated amortization, and net amounts.
  - 2021 totals: Gross $80.984B; Accumulated amortization $(55.838)B; Net $25.146B (finite-lived net $20.714B; indefinite-lived $4.432B).
  - 2020 totals: Gross $80.830B; Accumulated amortization $(52.493)B; Net $28.337B (finite-lived net $23.762B; indefinite-lived $4.575B).
  - Key finite-lived component is developed technology rights (2021 net $19.614B vs. 2020 $22.508B).

- Period changes and drivers:
  - Gross carrying amount increased primarily due to $500 million of capitalized Comirnaty sales milestones owed to BioNTech, partially offset by adverse foreign currency translation.
  - Net identifiable intangibles decreased mainly due to amortization, partially offset by the Comirnaty milestone capitalization.

- Category descriptions and examples:
  - Developed technology rights: Acquired rights to developed technology (develop, use, market, sell). Portfolio spans many therapeutic areas. Significant assets include Xtandi, Prevnar 13/Prevenar 13 (Infant and Adult), Braftovi/Mektovi, Premarin, Eucrisa, Orgovyx, Zavicefta, Tygacil, Bavencio, Merrem/Meronem, and Comirnaty. Includes post-approval milestone payments under alliances.
  - Brands: Tradenames and know-how. Indefinite-lived examples: Medrol, Depo-Medrol. Finite-lived examples: Zavedos, Depo-Provera.
  - IPR&D: R&D assets not yet approved in a major market; classified as indefinite-lived until approval or abandonment. Not amortized during development; upon approval, reclassified to finite-lived and amortized; if abandoned, written off as impairment. Significant programs include a PARP inhibitor from the Medivation acquisition and assets from the Array acquisition. Noted as high-risk with expectation of future impairments.
  - Licensing agreements: Rights acquired (often out-licensing arrangements) to future royalties/milestones tied to partners’ development/commercialization, including assets from the Array acquisition. During development, treated as indefinite-lived (no amortization); upon major-market approval, reclassified to finite-lived and amortized; abandoned projects are impaired. Significant arrangements relate to oncology technologies in various development stages.

Outcomes could either restrict competitor entry or require competitor royalties; invalidations could allow additional competitors.

nodes.title: Legal Proceedings––Patent Litigation
nodes.heading: A1. Legal Proceedings––Patent Litigation
nodes.start_phrase: We are involved in suits relating to our patents, including but not limited to, those discussed below.
nodes.summary:
- Describes Pfizer’s approach to legal and environmental contingencies, including reliance on estimates, a $1 million disclosure threshold for governmental environmental sanctions, and criteria for identifying and disclosing “principal” matters based on quantitative and qualitative materiality factors.
- Outlines extensive patent litigation activity, primarily challenges by generic manufacturers to Pfizer’s and partners’ product, process, dosage-form, and formulation patents, as well as antitrust/unfair competition counterclaims.
- Notes participation in USPTO/EPO proceedings (inter partes review, post-grant review, re-examination, opposition) and the business impact of patent outcomes (potential market entry and sales erosion if invalidated; injunctions or royalties if upheld and infringed).
- Highlights pneumococcal vaccine patent challenges before the PTAB and in federal court; a September 2021 global settlement and license with one challenger; and ongoing challenges in the U.S. and abroad.
- Acknowledges exposure to third-party infringement claims (including against Hospira subsidiaries) with potential for significant or enhanced damages and/or injunctive relief if infringement is found.
- Summarizes plaintiff-side patent cases:
  - EpiPen: King (a Pfizer subsidiary) vs. Sandoz over epinephrine autoinjector patents expiring 2025.
  - Xeljanz (tofacitinib): multiple ANDA filers; separate actions against Aurobindo (active ingredient and polymorph), Sinotherapeutics (extended release), Teva (22 mg extended release), and Slayback (oral solution).
  - Inlyta (axitinib): suit against Glenmark over crystalline form patent expiring 2030.
  - Ibrance (palbociclib): actions against numerous generics for capsules (crystalline patent expiring 2034) and tablets challenging patents expiring 2023, 2027, 2034, and 2036; one settlement not material.
  - Eucrisa: suits against several generics challenging patents expiring 2026–2030.
- Details collaboration/licensing partner matter for Eliquis (with BMS): suits against numerous generics; Delaware court found 2026 and 2031 patents valid and infringed; Federal Circuit affirmed in 2021; some settlements not material.
- Introduces product liability litigation, including numerous cases alleging personal injury and economic loss related to Pfizer products.
- Describes asbestos-related liabilities tied to Warner-Lambert’s former American Optical unit, ongoing indemnification obligations, and multiple suits alleging exposure via products and facilities.
- Summarizes Effexor XR antitrust litigation: since 2011, class and other actions alleging delayed generic entry through patent listing/enforcement and a settlement; claims under federal and certain state laws seeking treble damages for direct and indirect purchasers from June 14, 2008 onward.

nodes.title: Legal Proceedings––Product Litigation
nodes.heading: A2. Legal Proceedings––Product Litigation
nodes.start_phrase:
We
 are defendants in numerous cases, including but not limited to those discussed below, related to our pharmaceutical and other products.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from Pfizer’s 2021 Form 10-K Notes detailing significant legal proceedings and contingencies, including patent/IP disputes, product litigation, collaboration partner matters, environmental, and other commercial/legal issues.

- Patent and Hatch-Waxman/ANDA disputes:
  - Tofacitinib oral solution: 2022 suit against Slayback alleging infringement of compound patent.
  - Inlyta (axitinib): Glenmark ANDA challenging crystalline form patent (expires 2030); Pfizer sued in D. Del.
  - Ibrance (palbociclib): Multiple 2020–2021 generic challenges to capsule and tablet patents (composition of matter expiring 2023/2027; method of use 2023; crystalline form 2034; tablet formulation 2036); Pfizer filed infringement actions; one generic settled.
  - Eucrisa: 2021 ANDAs challenging composition and method patents (expiring 2026, 2027, 2030); suits filed in D. Del.

- Collaboration/licensing partner matter:
  - Eliquis (with BMS): 25 generics challenged Orange Book patents (one expired 2019; others 2026, 2031). Suits filed in D. Del. and N.D.W. Va.; August 2020 ruling upheld validity/infringement of 2026 and 2031 patents; Federal Circuit affirmed September 2021; some settlements reached.

- Product litigation and antitrust:
  - Asbestos: Claims tied to historical American Optical products; Warner-Lambert/Pfizer indemnity obligations; numerous personal injury suits.
  - Effexor XR: Consolidated antitrust class actions in D.N.J. alleging delayed generic entry via patent actions/listings and settlement; earlier dismissals reversed by Third Circuit in 2017.
  - Lipitor: MDL in D.N.J. alleging delayed generic launch via Ranbaxy settlement and patent conduct; district dismissals (2013–2014) reversed by Third Circuit in 2017; related West Virginia state action.
  - EpiPen (direct purchasers): 2020 antitrust suit in D. Kan. alleging delayed generic entry via settlement with Mylan; 2021 dismissal without prejudice; amended complaint filed.
  - Nexium 24HR and Protonix: PPI kidney injury litigation consolidated in D.N.J.; GSK Consumer Healthcare JV indemnifies Pfizer for Nexium 24HR-related liabilities.
  - Docetaxel: Personal injury suits alleging permanent alopecia; federal MDL in E.D. La.; separate Mississippi AG consumer protection action seeking penalties/injunctive relief.
  - Zantac: Cancer risk litigation; federal MDL in S.D. Fla. with master personal injury, consumer class, and medical monitoring complaints; third-party payor RICO claim dismissed (on appeal to 11th Cir.); Canadian class actions; New Mexico and Baltimore suits; California JCCP established.
  - Chantix: 2021 putative class actions in U.S., Canada, Israel following nitrosamine-related recall; claims for economic loss and medical monitoring.

- Commercial and other matters:
  - Monsanto-related: Indemnities by New Monsanto and Solutia for Pharmacia’s former agricultural/chemical businesses, including environmental and PCB-related claims; ongoing defense and indemnification of Pharmacia.

- Environmental matters:
  - Wyeth Holdings/American Cyanamid Bound Brook, NJ site: Series of EPA Administrative Settlement Agreements and Consent Decrees (2011, 2015, 2019, 2021) governing interim and final remedies for main plant area and adjacent lagoons; Pfizer has accrued estimated remediation costs; additional CERCLA and related proceedings pending.

- Other litigation:
  - Contracts with Iraqi Ministry of Health: Anti-Terrorism Act suit alleging companies’ sales practices funded terrorist groups; district court dismissal (2020) reversed on appeal (Jan 2022); en banc review sought (Feb 2022).

  - Chantix/Champix: Putative class actions in U.S., Canada, and Israel following voluntary recall for nitrosamine (N-nitroso-varenicline) presence; claims for economic loss, damages, and medical monitoring.

- Commercial and other matters:
  - Monsanto-related indemnities: Corporate history of Former Monsanto, Solutia, Pharmacia, and New Monsanto; allocation and assumption of liabilities and indemnification obligations to Pharmacia (now Pfizer subsidiary) for agricultural and chemical business claims, including environmental and PCB-exposure matters.
  - Environmental matters: Long-running EPA remediation at Wyeth Holdings’ former American Cyanamid site in Bound Brook, NJ, with multiple Administrative Settlement Agreements and court-approved consent decrees covering interim and final remedies for the main plant area and adjacent lagoons; accruals recorded for estimated remediation costs; participation in other CERCLA and analogous proceedings.
  - Contracts with Iraqi Ministry of Health: Anti-Terrorism Act suit alleging companies, including Pfizer, indirectly funded terrorist organizations via MOH contracts; district court dismissal in 2020; appellate reversal in 2022 with en banc review sought.
  - Allergan indemnity (Kadian): Indemnity claims against Pfizer and King related to opioid product previously owned by King; case voluntarily discontinued without prejudice in January 2021.

  - Viatris securities litigation: Putative class action in Pennsylvania state court under the Securities Act of 1933 concerning disclosures in registration/prospectus for the Upjohn spin-off and combination with Mylan; claims for damages and equitable relief against Viatris, Pfizer, and certain current/former officers and directors.

- Government investigations:
  - Greenstone generics:
    - DOJ Antitrust Division investigation since 2017 into former Greenstone business, aligned with broader generics industry probe; document productions ongoing.
    - State Attorneys General multi-state antitrust actions consolidated in federal MDL (E.D. Pa.), alleging federal/state antitrust and consumer protection violations; additional 2020 complaint covering a new drug set; related private and county civil cases pending.
  - Subpoena on Quillivant XR manufacturing (SDNY, 2018): Records sought regarding relationship with a manufacturer and production of certain drugs, including Quillivant XR; productions made.

  - DOJ/SEC FCPA inquiries (2019): Informal requests regarding operations in Russia; productions made.
  - Reference to Docetaxel—Mississippi AG investigation noted elsewhere in product litigation section.

- General risk statement: Potential outcomes from government investigations include criminal charges, fines/penalties, business limitations, compliance agreements, reputational harm, and continued exposure to qui tam actions even absent government intervention.

As of December 31, 2021, the estimated fair value of indemnification obligations is included in financials and is not material. Following the Upjohn spin-off, Viatris agreed to assume and indemnify certain liabilities. Pfizer also guarantees some subsidiaries’ long-term debt.
- Commitments: As of December 31, 2021, legally binding commitments total $5.2 billion, including likely milestone payments and purchase obligations.
- Contingent consideration: Fair value totaled $697 million at December 31, 2021 ($135 million current, $563 million noncurrent) versus $689 million at December 31, 2020; change driven by fair value adjustments and milestone payments.
- Insurance: Mix of purchased insurance and self-insurance (including product liability). Significant uninsured or underinsured liabilities could materially affect cash flows or results.
- Segment information: Following prior restructuring (Consumer Healthcare JV in 2019; Upjohn spin-off in 2020), Pfizer reorganized at the start of fiscal Q4 2021 into two operating segments—Biopharma (reportable; six therapeutic areas: Oncology, Inflammation & Immunology, Rare Disease, Hospital, Vaccines, Internal Medicine) and PC1 (contract development/manufacturing and specialty APIs). Biopharma receives R&D and regulatory services from WRDM and GPD. Prior-period management reporting revised to conform.
- Other costs and activities: Certain costs are not allocated to segments, including WRDM and GPD expenses, corporate/enabling functions, manufacturing overhead not managed by segments, Consumer Healthcare JV earnings, purchase accounting adjustments, acquisition-related items, and significant non-routine items (e.g., legal charges, restructuring, investment gains/losses). PC1 and, through July 2019, Consumer Healthcare are reported in Other business activities.
- Assets: Managed on a total company basis; no segment asset reporting. Total assets were $181 billion at December 31, 2021 and $154 billion at December 31, 2020.

nodes.summary:
The excerpt is from Pfizer’s 2021 Form 10-K Note 17 (Segment, Geographic and Other Revenue Information) and outlines how the company reports and evaluates performance after recent portfolio changes. Key points include:

- Operating structure and segments: Following the 2019 Consumer Healthcare JV and the 2020 Upjohn spin-off, Pfizer operated as a single segment through Q4 2020. Beginning in fiscal Q4 2021, Pfizer reorganized into two operating segments—Biopharma (innovative medicines and vaccines across Oncology, Inflammation & Immunology, Rare Disease, Hospital, Vaccines, and Internal Medicine) and PC1 (a global contract development and manufacturing organization and specialty API supplier). Biopharma is the only reportable segment; prior periods were revised to conform.

- Roles and unallocated costs: Commercial activities sit within each segment, while global platform functions support R&D, manufacturing, and supply. Biopharma receives R&D services from WRDM (early research, proof-of-concept, medical/safety) and GPD (clinical development, regulatory). Certain costs are not allocated to segments, including:
  • WRDM and GPD expenses (including upfront/milestone payments)
  • Corporate and Other Unallocated (corporate enabling functions, manufacturing overhead not managed by segments, interest, investment gains/losses, share of Consumer Healthcare JV earnings)
  • Purchase accounting adjustments, acquisition-related items, and “certain significant items” (e.g., pension actuarial gains/losses, JV gains, restructuring, legal matters, asset impairments, equity security gains/losses)
  PC1 operating results (and, through July 31, 2019, Consumer Healthcare) are included in Other business activities.

- Assets: Managed on a total-company basis; no segment asset reporting. Total assets were $181 billion at December 31, 2021, and $154 billion at December 31, 2020.

- Selected financials by segment (2019–2021): The table provides revenues, earnings, and depreciation/amortization for Biopharma and Other business activities, plus reconciling items. 2021 totals: $81.3 billion in revenues; $24.3 billion in income from continuing operations before taxes; $5.2 billion in depreciation/amortization. Biopharma 2021 revenues were $79.6 billion. Biopharma earnings include dividend income from ViiV ($166 million in 2021). Notes explain shared production facilities and allocation of depreciation.

- Significant items detail: 
  • 2021 included a $2.1 billion IPR&D charge (Trillium), $1.3 billion in restructuring/implementation costs and additional depreciation, and $1.1 billion in upfront/milestones, partly offset by $1.6 billion pension gains and $1.3 billion equity securities gains. 
  • 2020 included $1.7 billion asset impairments, $1.1 billion pension losses, and $791 million restructuring/related costs. 
  • 2019 included an $8.1 billion gain on the Consumer Healthcare JV completion, $2.8 billion asset impairments, and $750 million pension/postretirement losses.

- Geographic revenue breakdown: 2021 revenues by region—U.S. $29.7B; Developed Europe $18.3B; Developed Rest of World $12.5B; Emerging Markets $20.7B. The U.S. is the only country exceeding 10% of total revenue; Japan is the largest market outside the U.S. (9% in 2021). Revenues exceeded $500 million in 21 countries outside the U.S. in 2021.

- Comirnaty (COVID-19 vaccine) sales: Pfizer and BioNTech have supply agreements worldwide, selling primarily to governments/government-sponsored customers, including European Commission–negotiated agreements (Nov 2020, Feb and May 2021) under which each EU member state orders and pays directly.

- Significant customers/channels: Prescription products are sold mainly to wholesalers and also directly to retailers, hospitals, clinics, government agencies, and pharmacies. In the U.S., vaccines are sold to the federal government, CDC, wholesalers, provider offices, retail pharmacies, and integrated delivery networks; outside the U.S., vaccines are sold to government and non-government institutions.

- COVID-19 vaccine (Comirnaty) commercialization:
  - Global supply agreements with governments, including EC framework; Pfizer sells directly to governmental and sponsored customers; EU member states place and pay for their own orders.

- Customer concentration:
  - U.S. wholesalers as % of total revenues: McKesson 9% (2021), 16% (2020), 15% (2019); AmerisourceBergen 7%, 14%, 11%; Cardinal Health 5%, 10%, 9%.
  - Three wholesalers comprised 24%/30%/25% of trade A/R at 12/31/21, 12/31/20, 12/31/19.
  - U.S. government represented 13% of 2021 revenues and 12% of trade A/R (primarily Comirnaty).

- Major product and therapeutic area revenues (2021 unless noted):
  - Biopharma revenues: $79.6b.
  - Vaccines $42.6b, driven by Comirnaty $36.8b (vs. $154m in 2020) and Prevnar family $5.27b.
  - Oncology $12.33b: Ibrance $5.44b; Xtandi alliance $1.19b; Inlyta $1.00b; others.
  - Internal Medicine $9.33b: Eliquis alliance/direct $5.97b; Premarin $563m.
  - Hospital $7.30b: includes anti-infectives and Paxlovid $76m (launched late 2021).
  - Inflammation & Immunology $4.43b: Xeljanz $2.46b; Enbrel (ex-U.S./Canada) $1.19b.
  - Rare Disease $3.54b: Vyndaqel/Vyndamax $2.02b; BeneFIX $438m; Genotropin $389m.

  - Upjohn spin-off/combination with Mylan to form Viatris (Nov 16, 2020); Mylan-Japan collaboration terminated (Dec 21, 2020). These and Meridian (sold Dec 31, 2021) reflected as discontinued operations.
  - 4Q21 reorganization into two operating segments: Biopharma and PC1 (contract manufacturing, including $320m Comirnaty-related manufacturing for BioNTech in 2021; API sales; transitional supply to legacy businesses like Viatris).

- Remaining performance obligations (Comirnaty):
  - $34.4b contracted at 12/31/21 (excludes contracts <1 year): expected recognition $22.3b in 2022; $11.8b in 2023; $265m in 2024.

- Deferred revenues (Comirnaty advances):
  - $3.3b at 12/31/21 ($3.0b current; $249m noncurrent) vs. $957m at 12/31/20 (all current).

  - Deferred revenue for other products not significant.

- Exhibit 4.24: Description of securities registered under Exchange Act Section 12.
  - Capital stock: up to 12 billion authorized shares of common stock (par $0.05), one vote per share, dividend and liquidation rights, NYSE: PFE; up to 27 million authorized shares of preferred stock with Board-designated terms.
  - Anti-takeover provisions: limitations on stockholder-called special meetings (10% threshold), no stockholder action by written consent, Board authority to set board size and fill vacancies, and ability to issue preferred/rights; DGCL Section 203 restrictions on business combinations with interested stockholders.
- Description of debt securities (euro notes):
  - 0.250% Notes due 2022 (€1.0 billion) and 1.000% Notes due 2027 (€750 million), interest payable annually on March 6; denominations of €100,000 and €1,000 increments; payments via Euroclear/Clearstream; fallback U.S. dollar payments if euro unavailable.
  - Payment of additional amounts (gross-up) for certain U.S. withholding taxes, subject to standard exceptions.
  - Ranking: unsecured, unsubordinated, pari passu with other unsecured unsubordinated debt; listed on NYSE.
  - Covenants: limited; no protections for leverage, liens, guarantees, or sale-leasebacks beyond basic merger/consolidation provisions; ability to issue fungible additional notes if no default.
  - Redemption: make-whole optional redemption prior to defined par call windows; par call within 1 month (2022 notes) or 3 months (2027 notes) of maturity; tax redemption right; no sinking fund.
  - Book-entry only through Euroclear/Clearstream; procedures for secondary market settlement; limited circumstances for exchange into certificated notes.
  - Indenture mechanics: majority-consent amendments with core term protections requiring each holder’s consent; defined events of default, acceleration and rescission thresholds; trustee rights/indemnification; and defeasance options upon deposit of cash/government securities.
- Exhibit 21: Extensive list of subsidiaries as of December 31, 2021, spanning numerous jurisdictions and including major acquired platforms (e.g., Hospira, Wyeth, Medivation, Array, Trillium) and global operating, manufacturing, R&D, and holding entities.
- Exhibit 23: KPMG LLP consent to incorporation by reference of audit and ICFR reports into specified Pfizer registration statements (Forms S-8, S-4, and S-3 ASR).
